## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag does not take its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, which the project's CLI flag rules require of every new flag, so CI cannot set exclusions through the environment; the exclusion logic itself is covered by the added tests.

## Changes
Adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option that `collect` uses to skip files whose basename matches any pattern, logging each skipped path. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds unit and end-to-end tests plus a text fixture.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — Running in CI with `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and no `--exclude` flag still archives `.log` files, because the default is the literal `[]`. `.claude/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5` says: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot exclude files, which breaks the project rule for new flags. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choose and document a separator for multiple globs, update the `docs/flags.md:7` default column, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with an environment case.
